newsitem.title: UK: Man sees 1997 EU sugar beet unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Man sees 1997 EU sugar beet unchanged.

text.p: The area sown to sugar beet in the European Union should total 2.03 million hectares in 1997/98, unchanged from 1996/97, trade house E D & F Man said on Tuesday.
This represents a revision from Man's previous estimate, made a month ago, which showed a rise of 1.2 per cent to 2.05 million hectares.

In France, the area under cultivation is now expected to be a little lower, Man said. Latest projections from the French intervention board FIRS show a 0.5 per cent decrease in area to 420,000 hectares, it said.
Area in Germany is expected to be about 1.5 per cent down, to 508,687 hectares, rather than up by a few hundred hectares as initially suggested, Man said.

"The downward adjustments in area have resulted in a revision in our estimates for EU beet area to an unchanged level from last year, compared to the 1.2 per cent increase estimated previously," Man said.

Man notes worries over dry weather in France and the UK. In France, "by April 25 only 40 per cent of the beets were showing above the ground and rain over the following weekend was gratefully received," Man said.
It also cites problems with night frosts, "although these have only been marginal and only minimal re-sowing was required."
